question.problem: If $\alpha \beta =-8$ and $b\cdot a=\frac{15}{2}$, then what is $(\alpha a)\cdot (\beta b)+12?$
question.worked_solution:
Using the fact that the dot product is linear in both variables, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(\alpha a)\cdot (\beta b)+12 & =\alpha (a\cdot \beta b)+12 \\  & =\alpha \beta (a\cdot b)+12.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, using that the dot product is symmetric, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha \beta (a\cdot b)+12 & =\alpha \beta (b\cdot a)+12.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the values for $\alpha \beta $ and $b\cdot a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha \beta (b\cdot a)+12 & =(-8)\cdot \frac{15}{2}+12 \\  & =-60+12 \\  & =-48\end{aligned}
$$
